title: Firecrawl Alexandria and the Developer Index Are Now in ChatGPT and Codex
summary: The Firecrawl plugin now gives ChatGPT and Codex access to Firecrawl Alexandria: 100+ official data providers plus Firecrawl's own Research, Developer, and Government indexes. Find a tool, check what it costs, and pull the data without leaving the conversation.
body_markdown:
Firecrawl Alexandria is now available inside the[ChatGPT plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl) . ChatGPT and Codex can reach 100+ data providers and Firecrawl's own indexes, alongside the live web they already search.


## What is Firecrawl Alexandria?


Ask ChatGPT about a company's latest quarterly filing today and it searches the web, finds a page discussing the filing, and summarizes that page. You get a secondhand account of the numbers. The filing itself sits in a provider API the model has no way to call.


That limit shapes what agents are good for. They answer well when the open web has already written up a subject, and poorly when the answer turns on a primary source: what a series actually reported last quarter, what a regulator filed, what a dataset records. That information exists in structured form behind provider APIs, and an agent's only route to it has been whatever a blog post happened to quote.


[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://www.firecrawl.dev/alexandria?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=alexandria-chatgpt-codex) gives the agent that source directly, under agreement with the providers who maintain it. One request finds it, shows what it holds and what it costs, and pulls the data.


Without Firecrawl Alexandria With Firecrawl Alexandria


**What the agent reads** A page that discusses the data The provider's own record


**Coverage** Whatever the open web has written up 100+ official providers, plus Firecrawl's Research, Developer, and Government indexes


**Finding a source** Search, then hope a page quoted the number One request finds the source and reports what it holds


**Providers** Earn nothing from the answer Paid under agreement when your agent pulls their data


\[ Firecrawl Alexandria evals \]


Across 845 tasks with the same model, the same prompts and blind AI judging, agents using Firecrawl Alexandria scored


21% higher


on answer quality than agents using built-in web tools.


[Install the plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)


## How to use Firecrawl Alexandria in ChatGPT and Codex


Firecrawl Alexandria follows three steps: find a tool, check what it needs, then run it. You ask a question and the plugin walks those steps for you.


Ask for something the open web answers badly:


```text
Find   remote   software   engineering   jobs   posted   in   the   past   week.   Include   salaries   where   available   and   application   links.
```


ChatGPT searches for relevant tools, reads the inputs and price on the one it picks, and calls it. You see what it chose and what the data cost.


The same pattern covers research papers, company filings, government spending records, podcast transcripts, package registries, and real estate. When no provider fits, the plugin falls back to web search and scraping, so a gap in provider coverage doesn't dead-end the question.


You can also ask what exists before committing to anything:


```text
List   the   data   providers   that   cover   federal   contract   awards,   with   the   price   each   one   charges   per   call   in   Firecrawl.
```


None of that costs anything. ChatGPT comes back with the providers, their capabilities, and their prices, and you decide whether to spend anything.


## The Developer Index in Codex


Codex gets the[Developer Index](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/developer?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=alexandria-chatgpt-codex) , built over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation.


The answer to a question like this usually sits in a README, an issue thread, or a merged fix rather than in a blog post. The Developer Index searches that material directly and hands Codex the matching passages.


```text
How   do   I   add   pydantic   with   uv   instead   of   pip?
```


## Terms and billing


**Discovery is free, execution is billed.** Asking what data exists, reading a tool's inputs, and checking its price cost nothing. You pay the tool's listed price when it runs.


**Some providers need their terms accepted first.** Accepting a provider's terms binds your whole organization, so by default an admin accepts them in the[dashboard](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=data-sources&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=alexandria-chatgpt-codex) . When a provider needs this, ChatGPT shows you the terms and points to the page.


## Getting started


If you already have the[official ChatGPT plugin](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-official-chatgpt-plugin) installed, Firecrawl Alexandria is live in your next conversation.


If you don't:


1. Open ChatGPT
2. Install the[Firecrawl plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)
3. Connect your Firecrawl account when prompted


Then ask for a quarterly filing and watch which provider it reaches for.


- [Browse the provider catalog](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/alexandria?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=alexandria-chatgpt-codex)
- [Read the Firecrawl Alexandria docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alexandria?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=alexandria-chatgpt-codex)
